name: Orient Bell Ltd
title: Orient Bell Ltd-$ - 530365 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Orient Bell Q1 FY27 revenue rose 42.8% YoY to INR203 crores, with EBITDA margin at 8.7% and a record 39.7% gross margin.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 42.8% YoY to INR203 crores on 22.9% volume growth and about 15.9% higher ASP, with EBITDA up to INR17.6 crores from INR5.6 crores. Management attributed the quarter to Morbi shutdowns (late March to mid-May) that opened a supply gap, plus its own demand-generation push and dealer sell-out support. The company remains debt-free, reports a working capital cycle of 18 days, and is weighing deployment of its cash. Management declined to give any revenue or margin guidance.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: South volume grew about 37% and West about 60% in Q1; retail has grown faster than enterprise in recent quarters.

segments.name: Projects
segments.commentary: Project revenue was 18% of Q1 sales, including retail-sourced projects above 3,000 meters and key account projects.

segments.name: GVT (glazed vitrified tiles)
segments.commentary: GVT was about 47% of Q1 sales by value; about 15-20% of GVT came from Dora plant, bulk from SKD, and a low single-digit share from Morbi.

segments.name: Tile adhesives (Masterbond)
segments.commentary: Early-stage, cash-and-carry business with INR2.5 crores of sales in Q1, currently scaling in North and part of East India.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give revenue or margin guidance; it cited volatile Middle East and gas-price conditions.
Current gas prices are broadly stable, with July close to Q1 levels; no price cuts taken yet, with management monitoring the market.
Management said it is watching the market and will be competitive if selling prices soften.
Company is holding INR75 crores-plus in cash and plans to announce deployment of the larger part over the next three to four months.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation rose to 73% in Q1 from 64% in Q4 and about 60% blended in FY26.
Plan to invest around INR10 crores to convert 1 million meters of existing ceramic capacity to GVT.
Small capex of about INR15 crores over the next four to five months, internally financed, covering line conversion, digital printing machine replacement and polishing machines.
Next phase of manufacturing expansion under evaluation; decision expected in two to three months.
No plans to enter bathware; focus on tiles plus adhesives.
demand_pricing: Price increase of about 18-19% taken versus pre-war levels, with almost all of it realised.
Sell-out was about 40% of primary sales in Q1 versus 26% last year; DSO improved by 5 days.
Morbi-Organised gap narrowed to INR50-55 from about INR100 on comparable products, which benefits organised players.
Dealers are adding suppliers in other geographies to reduce dependence on Morbi.

Gas: Q1 average about INR60 per unit; Sikandrabad (North) moved from INR44-45 pre-war to INR60-62. Morbi exports fell to about INR800 crores a month average in April-May versus INR1,500-1,600 crores earlier.

qa_highlights.question: How much price increase was taken in Q1 and are prices sustainable as gas prices fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Price increase of about 18-19% versus pre-war, almost fully realised; no cuts yet, with management watching gas and Morbi pricing.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 23% volume growth and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Morbi supply gap during the shutdown plus OBL's demand generation, with about 40% sell-out support to dealers and 24/7 TV advertising; management pointed to input KPIs rather than guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Dora plant utilisation, and share of GVT and EBITDA from it?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant-level utilisation is misleading due to inter-plant transfers; South and West growth was used as proxy. About 15-20% of GVT comes from Dora.

qa_highlights.question: Guidance for FY27 revenue and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Company policy is no guidance on revenue or margins; management cited positive quarter-on-quarter KPIs only.

qa_highlights.question: Use of about INR75 crores of cash?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR15 crores of internally financed capex over four to five months; the larger part is to be invested in the business, with a decision in three to four months.

qa_highlights.question: Tile adhesives progress and bathware plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Adhesives generated INR2.5 crores in Q1 on a cash-and-carry basis, expanding from North to East; no bathware plans.

risks_watch: Gas and propane prices remain volatile; any fall could force price cuts, and management has not yet committed to holding prices.
Morbi capacity is back at full run-rate since mid-May, so the supply-gap tailwind may fade.
Exports from Morbi remain depressed by higher freight costs (5-6x to Gulf).
Deployment of about INR75 crores of cash and the next manufacturing expansion are undecided.
summary.management_tone: Confident on results and market share, but cautious and non-committal on outlook, repeatedly declining guidance and calling pricing and gas costs too volatile to forecast.
key_quotes: Our demand generation initiatives have ensured a sellout of approximately 40% of the primary sales volume in Q1 versus 26% sellout last year.
As a result, we achieved our highest ever gross margin of 39.7% during this quarter.
As a policy, we do not give any guidance for future.

growth.why: Management gives no revenue or margin guidance; Q1 revenue rose 42.8% YoY on a temporary Morbi supply gap, utilisation is 73%, and the modest capex (about INR25 crore total) is mostly conversion rather than large new capacity, so the outlook is unclear.
